newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Airport's fate to be decided soon. The government is re-evaluating the costs and benefits of the proposed new international airport at Nong Ngu Hao and will decide soon whether to continue with the project, Deputy Prime Minister Korn Tabaransi said yesterday. Korn, the policy supervisor of the Transport and Communications Ministry, said his team will discuss the fate of Nong Ngu Hoa airport, a 200 billion baht development, with Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh at a scheduled meeting next month. (THE NATION)

- Eight officials face arrest in connection with the Tha Chana logging scandal in which Democrat MP Suthep Thueksuban has been implicated. Suthep, a Surathani MP, is also likely to face arrest this week, according to a senior police officer.

Deputy police director-general Salang Bunnag, in his capacity as director of Forest, Poaching Prevention and Supression Task Force, has signed an arrest warrant for the eight officials. (BANGKOK POST)

- The severe stock market slump is setting the stage for mergers and acquisitions of listed companies, particularly those that are under-performing the market, according to investment bankers. An analayst from Premier Finance and Securities said under-priced stocks are expected to have lower than-expected earnings per share growth and suffer more from the liquidity crunch. (THE NATION)

- Analysts cautious over indication of recovery. The Thai economy may be emerging from the doldrums. Although few consumers are rushing to take out a new home or car loan, some macro-economic indicators say a recovery may well be in hand.
The latest figures from the Bank of Thailand for three indicators - the private investment index and M1 Money supply figures - are pointing to a slight pickup in the economy. (BANGKOK POST)
